design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST
The caller asks one money question - what calling off next Saturday's dinner will cost, on the books today - and the
number she is owed is the product of three things she never mentions: a multi-factor calculation (eleven declared
factors across the two problems), a reconciliation of an event ledger carrying five bookings, four deposits, one
guarantee, two earlier cancellations and their charges, and a set of if-else ladders keyed on dates, counts, room
set-up, a request log and another product line's order book. Nothing can be guessed from the tool list: both writes are
hidden task tools, and the difficulty is entirely in reading the published rules, finding the records and getting two
figures exactly right, in an order the policy dictates.

SCOPE CLAIMED AND WHAT REMAINS
Task 0 claims banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value (the contracted value standing at notice, on
confirm_event_cancellation_0abc9941) and banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment (the cancellation charge, on
post_cancellation_charge_5262dfa3). Nothing was occupied before it. It deliberately leaves the whole settlement half of
the charter free for task 1: the deposit application against a bill (banquet_deposit_applied) and the client's own
settlement payment (banquet_payment_posted), together with the base policies banquet_settlement_terms,
banquet_payment_terms and banquet_agg_deposit_and_diary_pooling's deposit half. Task 0 touches banquet_cancellation_terms
and banquet_booking_terms only; task 1 touches neither of those as a governing policy of its writes.

THE STEP 0 DRAW
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/tasks/banquet_event_desk --tasks 2 printed:
{"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [5, 6]} and
{"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}.
Task 0 was designed to that draw: one prerequisite problem, and the two computations carry 6 factors
(banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value) and 5 factors (banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment).

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root problem: banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment - the charge the caller rings about.
Prerequisite problem: banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value - the client's own written notice of cancellation, carrying
the contracted event value standing at that day.
Edge: kind value_input, gate contracted_value (a compute binding of the root), form state.
Prerequisite sentence (in the root policy's own rule, verbatim): "The charge for a cancelled event is not fixed until
the event ledger carries, for that booking, a cancellation entry recording the day written notice was given and the
contracted event value standing at that day."
Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "not until", joining this policy's own result (the charge for a cancelled
event) to what it waits on; the affirmative contrapositive - "the charge for a cancelled event is fixed only once the
event ledger carries, for that booking, a cancellation entry recording the day written notice was given and the
contracted event value standing at that day" - carries the same result, the same waited-on state and the same scope,
with no condition added, dropped or split. The negated direction is the one the desk uses for a charge that waits on the
client's notice. (2) The XX side is a record-visible state - a kind of entry standing on the event ledger, with the two
fields it must carry - named in the words the ledger and its finder use, with no action and no performer. (3) It names
no tool, no policy id and no code token. (4) Its strength matches the edge exactly: a hard "not until", one kind of
entry, one booking.
State form was possible and used: exactly one write in this difficulty puts a banquet_booking_cancelled entry on the
ledger, namely the target tool of banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value, so the reader who sees the state is missing can
resolve the hop uniquely. Derivation a solver performs: the sentence says the charge waits on a cancellation entry with
a notice day and a standing value; the ledger read shows five bookings and only two cancellation entries, neither under
BQ-418206; the other policy's rule says what its result is - the contracted event value standing at the moment written
notice of cancellation is given - and the desk's rules put the ending of a confirmed event in the client's own hands;
therefore the client must register her cancellation first, and the charge is worked afterwards.
Unmet at frozen_time: no banquet_booking_cancelled row exists for BQ-418206 (initial_state.banquet_ledger rows under
that reference are the booking entry, two deposits and the guarantee); the cancellation entries that do stand carry
BQ-395512 and BQ-409883.
Topological order: banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value then banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment.
Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the client's write moves the charge from 53211.65 to 7320.00.
The customer never mentions the prerequisite (see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint) and no tool validates it (see
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Write 1, subject banquet_booking_cancelled. Governing base policy: banquet_cancellation_terms. Gate cancellable_state
("Once an event has been delivered it can no longer be cancelled...") - authority system_record, pre-action, correlated
on banquet_ledger.booking_reference which binds to the tool's booking_reference argument. Satisfied: the agreement
stands active and the ledger carries no banquet_event_delivered row for BQ-418206 at all, so the event has not been
delivered. Gate charge_posting_window does not apply to this subject (applies_to is banquet_cancellation_charge_posted).
Write 2, subject banquet_cancellation_charge_posted. Same governing policy; both gates apply.
cancellable_state as above. charge_posting_window is a time gate: anchor event "the day the client gives written notice
of cancellation", anchor source banquet_ledger.notice_given_date, relation not_after, duration params.
charge_posting_window_days = 5, unit calendar days counted from the day after notice, boundary inclusive. At frozen_time
notice is 2026-09-22 and the charge is raised 2026-09-22, nought days into a five-day window. Negative boundary: notice
on 2026-09-16 would put the last in-time day at 2026-09-21, so a charge raised today would be out of time; notice on
2026-09-17 puts the boundary day at today itself and the inclusive boundary keeps it in time.
Inherited and not overridden anywhere: the free-cancellation window governing first, the deposit rules of
banquet_deposit_terms, the guarantee rules, the diary ceiling of banquet_agg_deposit_and_diary_pooling, and the
agreement-state rules. Five clauses are overridden, each declared in the charter: banquet_booking_terms' minimum-spend
sentence (replaced by the room-hire treatment of a value standing short of the minimum); banquet_cancellation_terms'
four-band sentence (replaced by the notice percentage and the repeat percentage added together and held to one hundred);
banquet_cancellation_terms' "only the balance is invoiced" sentence (replaced by raising the full charge and setting
deposit money against it at settlement, which is what the tool's own parameter records); banquet_guarantee_terms'
deemed-guarantee sentence (replaced by reading no guarantee where no confirmed guarantee entry stands, which is what
every fall-through tier of the first computation does); and banquet_combination_venue_interaction's same-room
exclusivity (replaced by the same-day test, on the ground the base sentence itself gives - the room is held by the
booking, and it is held for the whole of the event day - because no record on either side carries a room: the catering
order carries a site code and the agreement a venue code).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Target object: booking BQ-418206 under banquet agreement 093e5fcc-4d34-464a-b9c7-e4ed66830b6c at venue VN-312 - the seated dinner on 2026-09-27. The
correlation key the desk works on is booking_reference, which both tools carry. Rows that belong to it: the booking
entry (40800.00, 240 guests, seated rounds), the two deposits (12240.00 each), the confirmed guarantee (268 guests,
45560.00). Rows on the same agreement that are deliberately not part of it: the December reception BQ-421884 and the
February dinner BQ-423170 with their deposits (they are the remaining diary, counted only as a number), and the two
cancelled bookings BQ-395512 and BQ-409883 with their charges and deposit applications (counted only as the twelve-month
repeat reading). The catering order CO-551402 is correlated by service day: it is served on the event's own day,
2026-09-27; CO-549118 on 2026-09-26 and CO-544870 on 2026-09-03 are not, and are the planted near-misses.

FACTOR CARD - banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value (6 factors, result 69802.20, whole baseline 50726.00)
1 committed_food_value (method, multi-source, cross-difficulty: catering). Tier taken: a confirmed guarantee entry
  stands and catering orders stand for the event's own day. Evidence: the guarantee row (45560.00) and the catering
  order CO-551402 (3250.00, service_date 2026-09-27) on the client's active Delivered Buffet Account. Baseline reading:
  the booking entry's own estimate, 40800.00, giving 60030.00. Near-miss: CO-549118, 1180.00 on the set-up day.
2 contracted_room_extras (parameter). Tier taken: the guarantee is built to seated rounds, so the audio-visual package
  850.00 and the dance floor 650.00 stand. Baseline: no extras, giving 68302.20.
3 room_rental_standing (parameter). Tier taken: the booking entry's 40800.00 reaches the 12000.00 waiver spend, so no
  rental stands. Baseline: the printed 950.00 rental, giving 70752.20.
4 contracted_hours_counted (method, multi-source). Tier taken: a guarantee stands and its 268 exceeds the 240 the
  booking was taken at, so 5.0 + 4.0 + 2.0 = 11.0 hours are counted. Baseline: the 5.0 included hours, giving 65518.20.
5 contracted_staffing (parameter, multi-source). Tier taken: a guarantee stands and 268 reaches the smallest guest
  count 60, so 17 members at 42.00 for 11.0 hours = 7854.00. Baseline: no contracted staffing, giving 61948.20.
6 bar_element_standing (parameter, multi-source). Tier taken: seated rounds with 268 covers, so half the 1800.00 bar
  minimum, 900.00. Baseline: no bar element, giving 68902.20.
No field in the schema stamps any of these outcomes; every tier is read from ledger rows, a date span, a set-up value
and another category's order ledger.

FACTOR CARD - banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment (5 factors, result 53211.65, whole baseline 41881.32)
1 notice_percentage (parameter, 4 tiers). Tier taken: notice inside seven days (2026-09-22 to 2026-09-27 is five days),
  so 90. Baseline: the thirty-to-seven percentage 60, giving 37506.15.
2 repeat_cancellation_percentage (parameter, multi-source not required here). Tier taken: two cancellation charges
  inside the twelve months ending today (2026-08-28 and 2026-09-10), so the higher uplift 10. Baseline: none, giving
  47976.49.
3 remaining_diary_relief (method). Tier taken: two confirmed events neither delivered nor cancelled remain, so the
  charge is reduced by a quarter. Baseline: the banded charge as worked, giving 70662.20.
4 security_standdown (parameter, multi-source). Tier taken: 268 guests pass the 250 threshold and notice fell inside
  seven days, so 52.00 for 5.0 hours = 260.00. Baseline: none, giving 52951.65.
5 diary_work_charge (parameter). Tier taken: the event request log carries one approved date change and no approved
  venue change, so 600.00. Near-miss: two further requests on the log are declined. Baseline: none, giving 52611.65.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS
The booking entry and its guarantee carry the estimate, the working count, the guaranteed count, the event day and the
set-up: remove the guarantee and factors 1, 2, 4 and 6 of the first computation fall to their baselines while factor 5,
contracted staffing, takes its second tier instead (the working count of 240 at one server per 16 for the 5.0
included hours, 3150.00) and factor 3, the room rental, is untouched by the guarantee and stays at its waiver
tier; the result on that world is 52926.00, not the 49776.00 a fall to every baseline would give. The two
deposits keep the agreement's deposit balance honest and are what a solver must not confuse with the contracted value.
The December and February bookings are the remaining diary that buys the quarter reduction; delete one and the charge
rises to the tenth-reduction tier. The two cancelled bookings with their charges and deposit applications are the
twelve-month repeat reading; delete one and the uplift falls from 10 to 5. The three event requests are the diary work
charge and its two declined near-misses. The catering agreement and its three orders are the cross-difficulty evidence,
one on the event day and two off it. No cache field exists on this holding, so no cache trap is designed; the
agreement's two balances are exactly the sums of their account deltas and are stated as such in seed_consistency.

WHAT A CARELESS AGENT GETS WRONG
Reading the booking's estimate instead of the guarantee (60030.00 at the first write); adding the working lunch boxes of the day
before as well (71241.80, the food value becoming 45560.00 + 3250.00 + 1180.00 = 49990.00); charging the printed room rental although the waiver is met; counting the included hours
only; missing the repeat uplift and settling for the 90 percent band; forgetting that the quarter reduction is read on
what still stands in the diary after this cancellation is registered; taking the declined date change as approved;
and above all raising the charge first, which reads another booking's cancellation entry and yields 7320.00.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate the profile by company name, verify on the two details the caller reads out, read the agreement (package, state,
venue), read the whole event ledger, read the event request log, read the catering agreement and its orders. Work the
contracted value standing at notice: 45560.00 + 3250.00 = 48810.00 food, + 1500.00 extras, + 0.00 rental, + 7854.00
staffing, + 900.00 bar, + 10738.20 service charge = 69802.20. Hand the cancellation to the client, who registers it
with that value. Then work the charge: 90 + 10 = 100 percent of 69802.20 = 69802.20, reduced by a quarter to 52351.65,
plus 260.00 security, plus 600.00 diary work = 53211.65, and raise it.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN
The handling-time recomputation was executed with the gate's own evaluator over initial_state plus the replayed gold
writes. Output: banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value result = 69802.2 with factor baselines 60030.0 / 68302.2 /
70752.2 / 65518.2 / 61948.2 / 68902.2 and whole baseline 50726.0; banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment result =
53211.65 with factor baselines 37506.15 / 47976.49 / 70662.2 / 52951.65 / 52611.65 and whole baseline 41881.32; the
same policy evaluated without the client's write gives 7320.0. Every figure above is that output, and every one differs
from gold, so no declared factor is decoration.

RULE / COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP
Forward: every binding that reads the world or chooses a branch quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis - the ledger
maxima and the catering sum quote the food-value paragraph, the set-up read and the extras ladder quote the extras
paragraph, the booking-entry value and the rental ladder quote the rental paragraph, the guarantee count and the hours
ladder quote the hours paragraph, the staffing ladder quotes the staffing paragraph, the covers read and the bar ladder
quote the bar paragraph, and on the charge side the notice span, the band, the twelve-month count, the uplift, the
diary count, the relief, the security and the diary work charge each quote their own sentences. Backward: every
load-bearing sentence of both rules is claimed by a binding - the rounding sentence by the final RND, the "held to one
hundred" by MN, the twelve-month window by within_months=12, the "neither delivered nor cancelled" by the three counts,
the "approved" filter by the request_status filter, the waiver and minimum-spend sentences by the rental ternary. The
only sentences without a binding are the two prerequisite sentences, which are the edge's normative text.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
With the extended yaml, compute, expected and gold masked, and only the rule prose that will be published, the tool
schemas, the records a finder returns and the caller's actual lines in view, the derivation runs: the charge waits on a
cancellation entry; none stands for this booking; the client must register it; its value is the contracted value
standing at notice, built from the guarantee plus the same-day catering, the seated-rounds extras, no rental, eleven
hours of staffing, half the bar minimum and the service charge = 69802.20; the charge is then 100 percent of that,
reduced by a quarter for the two events still in the diary, plus security and the diary work charge = 53211.65. Same
object, same order, same two numbers as gold; no second reading was found, because each ladder's tiers are disjoint as
stated and every quantity is named after the act it belongs to.

ROUND 2 - POLICY-TASK AUDIT DISPOSITIONS (revision 1 of audits/policy_task/banquet_event_desk/)
Every figure below was re-derived after the change with the gate's own evaluator; no scored value, factor baseline,
whole baseline or skip-the-edge figure moved (69802.20 / 53211.65; 60030.00, 68302.20, 70752.20, 65518.20, 61948.20,
68902.20; 50726.00; 37506.15, 47976.49, 70662.20, 52951.65, 52611.65; 41881.32; 7320.00).

F-2 / T0-F1 (RED, closed). Symptom: the rule said the service charge was worked on "that estimated value" - the booking
entry's estimate - while compute worked it on the committed food value, leaving 68040.00 standing against gold's
69802.20. Root cause: an antecedent never redirected when the food-value ladder was added. Change: the sentence now
reads "The service charge printed against the package is worked on the food and beverage value the contracted value is
built on", in the rule, in baseline.rule and in compute_basis.service_charge_usd alike; the quantity it names is the
one the second paragraph defines and the one compute uses. The baseline paragraph stays self-sufficient: with no factor
applied that value is the booking entry's estimate, 40800.00, so the computation document still yields 50726.00. Re-run:
COMPUTE OK, every figure unchanged.

F-8 / T0-F2 (RED, closed). Symptom: base absorbs a catering order into an event only for the same room on the same day;
the tier tested the day alone, and no record carries a room (the order carries site CS-318, the agreement venue VN-312),
leaving 65837.20 standing against 69802.20. Base is frozen, so the divergence is declared rather than removed: the
policy now carries an overwrite against banquet_combination_venue_interaction quoting its same-room sentence, replaced
by "The room a confirmed booking holds is held for the whole of the event day, so an order standing on the client's
corporate catering account for that day is food for that room, and the day alone settles it, whether or not the order
names the room." The ground is base's own - the room is held by the booking - and the replacement says outright which
test governs, so the base-literal reading no longer stands.

T0-F13 (RED, closed). Symptom: the only cross-difficulty evidence row was a 268-guest catering order on an active
Delivered Buffet Account, whose max_headcount is 120, which that charter refers to the banquet desk and never runs as
one order. Change: the row CO-551402 is re-seeded at 62 guests (Delivered Buffet Account admits 12 to 120) and renamed
"Partner Briefing Breakfast" - a briefing for part of the party, not the whole dinner - keeping amount_usd 3250.00, which
clears that level's 225.00 minimum order value. Nothing the banquet compute reads changed: the cross-difficulty factor
still reads XSUM over catering_orders.amount_usd for the event's own day, its evidence is still seeded, and
contracted_value_usd is still 69802.20. The two near-miss orders (40 and 60 guests) were already inside the same band.

T0-F14 (RED, closed). Two design_rationale assertions failed recomputation and are corrected above: the day-before
order counted as well gives 71241.80 (food value 45560.00 + 3250.00 + 1180.00 = 49990.00), not 70990.00, and it is the
working lunch boxes rather than a second breakfast; and removing the guarantee row drops factors 1, 2, 4 and 6 to their
baselines while factor 5 takes its second tier (240 covers at one server per 16 for the 5.0 included hours, 3150.00) and
factor 3 is untouched, giving 52926.00. Both recomputed with the charter's own evaluator.

T0-F15 (closed). The persona no longer supplies the determination the policy owes: "she says that was the partners'
briefing before the dinner, put on the catering account the way the office always does, and that where it lands on paper
is the desk's business rather than hers." She states the fact and leaves the judgement to the desk; the cited
required_user_inputs snippet moved with it.

F-6 (closed). Base's "Deposits held against the cancelled booking are set against the charge first, and only the balance
is invoiced" is now declared superseded on banquet_ext_cancellation_charge_assessment, replaced by "What is raised is the
full charge the cancelled booking carries, and deposit money standing against that booking is set against it when the
charge is settled rather than when it is raised" - which is what the tool's own parameter records and what the seeded
ledger shows twice.

F-7 (closed). Base's deemed guarantee is now declared superseded on banquet_ext_cancellation_notice_value, replaced by
"Where no confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking, the working count the booking was taken at is not read as a
guarantee in its place, and the contracted value is built on the booking entry's own estimate, with no guaranteed count
to dress the room or to price a bar against." The wording deliberately stops short of the staffing ladder, which has its
own no-guarantee tier on the working count.

F-5 and F-12 (closed). The three docstrings that pre-announced a later action were reworded to describe only their own
effect, and the money parameters now state the rounding the implementation performs (to the nearest cent, a half-cent to
the nearer even cent) instead of half away from zero.

F-3 (partially closed, remainder accepted). The one place where the rule contradicted itself - "The diary work already
done on the booking is charged on top as well", whose own tiers read the agreement's request log - now says "on the
agreement". The remaining booking-scope wording is accepted rather than rewritten: the DSL aggregates at agreement scope
by construction, the two readings coincide on this world (the target booking carries the maximum booked value 40800.00,
the maximum booked count 240 and, once written, the maximum cancelled value 69802.20), and rewriting the prerequisite
sentence - which the audit passed on all four points - to say "on the agreement" would weaken the edge the task rests on.

F-11 and T0-F16 (accepted). The method label of contracted_hours_counted was accepted by the audit and is unchanged; the
remaining charter-global observations carry no consequence on this world and are dispositioned in task 1's dossier where
they bear.
user_scenario:
Marta Okonkwo looks after workplace experience for Northvale Life Sciences and has spent three days on the phone to people whose diaries have fallen apart. She rings the event desk mid-morning, brisk and a little apologetic, with a spreadsheet open in front of her. The first thing she says is that the partner dinner on 27 September is not going ahead: the two board members it was built around are in Basel that week and the company will not run it without them. What she needs is to know what Northvale will be charged for pulling out this late, and to have whatever it costs standing against the account today rather than at the end of the quarter, because her finance director closes the September numbers on Friday and will not take a figure that arrives afterwards.

She is content for the desk to do the working out and says so plainly: she is not going to argue with the contract, she only needs the figure to be right and to be on the books. If the agent needs her to do something herself she will do it there and then, because she is at her desk with the file open.

She does not volunteer her details. Asked who is calling or how to find the account, she gives the company name, Northvale Life Sciences. Pressed for something more, she reads out her direct line, 4695204188, and the client account code printed on the last invoice, CA-33047. Asked for the billing postcode she says she would have to dig it out of the finance system and would rather not; asked when the profile was first opened she laughs and says that was well before her time. If the agent asks which event she means she says the seated dinner on 27 September, the one for a couple of hundred and sixty-odd partners, and that the booking reference on her paperwork is BQ-418206.

When the agent explains that calling the booking off is something Northvale has to do itself and offers to put it in front of her, she takes it without fuss and runs it while they are talking, saying the file is open anyway; if the agent asks her to read the confirmation back she does. If the agent quotes her a figure before anything is registered she says that is fine and waits. Once she hears that the cancellation is registered and the charge has been raised against the account, she asks only whether it will show on the September statement, takes a yes for an answer, thanks the agent and rings off.

If the agent asks whether Northvale would rather move the dinner than drop it, she says no: the whole point is that the people are not available and there is no other date this quarter. If the agent asks about the breakfast delivery ordered for that same morning, she says that was the partners' briefing before the dinner, put on the catering account the way the office always does, and that where it lands on paper is the desk's business rather than hers. She does not know what any of it costs and will not guess; asked for a figure she says that is exactly what she is ringing to find out.

seed_consistency.check: The agreement stands active on the Seated Banquet Package at venue VN-312, countersigned 2025-04-01 inside a 24-month term running to 2027-03-31, which is the term the package prints; every printed figure the two calculations use is read from that package column. Its deposit balance 44970.00 is exactly the deposits received (12240.00 + 12240.00 + 9450.00 + 11040.00 + 6720.00 + 5670.00 = 57360.00) less the deposits applied (6720.00 + 5670.00 = 12390.00), and its receivable balance 19110.00 is exactly the two cancellation charges raised (13440.00 + 5670.00) with no payment yet posted; both were raised inside the last month, so neither is past due and the 75-day credit hold threshold is nowhere near.

The target booking: confirmed 2026-05-18 for 2026-09-27 at the agreement's own venue VN-312, estimated at 40800.00 with a working count of 240, which sits between the package's smallest and largest guest counts (60 and 350) and is above its minimum food and beverage spend of 6500.00. It was confirmed 132 days ahead, well beyond the 30-day booking lead the package prints, and its event day matches the date change the desk approved for it.

First deposit on the target booking: 12240.00 received 2026-05-29, exactly 30 percent of the 40800.00 estimate as the package prints, and inside the 14 calendar days from the 2026-05-18 confirmation that the deposit due window allows.

Second deposit on the target booking: 12240.00 received 2026-09-04, exactly the 30 percent second instalment the package prints, paid before the 21 days ahead of the 2026-09-27 event day by which it falls due.

The confirmed guarantee: 268 guests given on 2026-09-19 for the 2026-09-27 event, pricing to 45560.00, which is 268 covers at the 170.00 per cover the 40800.00 estimate for 240 was taken at. It was given eight days ahead, inside the 96-hour guarantee deadline the package prints, and it raises rather than lowers the working count, which is the only direction a guarantee may move after the deadline.

A second confirmed event still to be served: a reception for 180 on 2026-12-04, estimated 31500.00, booked 2026-08-11 at the agreement's venue. It is one of the two events that keep the diary committed, and its count sits inside the package's guest range.
First deposit on the December reception: 9450.00 received 2026-08-20, exactly 30 percent of 31500.00 and inside the 14-day deposit due window from the 2026-08-11 confirmation.

A third confirmed event still to be served: a seated dinner for 210 on 2027-02-19, estimated 36800.00, booked 2026-09-01 at the agreement's venue, inside the term and inside the package's guest range.
First deposit on the February dinner: 11040.00 received 2026-09-10, exactly 30 percent of 36800.00 and inside the 14-day deposit due window from the 2026-09-01 confirmation.

A booking since cancelled: a theater-set event for 140 on 2026-09-20, estimated 22400.00, confirmed 2026-06-15. Its count and value sit inside the package, and it is the older of the two cancellations that the repeat reading counts.
Deposit on that cancelled booking: 6720.00 received 2026-06-26, exactly 30 percent of 22400.00 and inside the 14-day window from the 2026-06-15 confirmation.

The client's written notice on that booking: given and registered 2026-08-26 against an event day of 2026-09-20, 25 whole days, recording the 22400.00 contracted value standing at that day and the 140 guests standing on it.

The charge that answered it: 13440.00 raised 2026-08-28, two days after notice and so inside the five-day posting window, and exactly the 60 percent thirty-to-seven band on 22400.00 for notice 25 days out. It carries its own bill reference and is one of the two charges the twelve-month repeat reading counts.

The deposit held against that cancelled booking set against its charge: 6720.00 applied 2026-08-28 to the same bill reference the charge carries, which is the deposit not being returnable inside the 45-day refundable window.
The second booking since cancelled: a classroom-set event for 120 on 2026-10-10, estimated 18900.00, confirmed 2026-07-07, inside the package's guest range and lead time.
Deposit on that booking: 5670.00 received 2026-07-18, exactly 30 percent of 18900.00 and inside the 14-day window from the 2026-07-07 confirmation.

The client's written notice on it: given 2026-09-07 and registered 2026-09-08 against an event day of 2026-10-10, 33 whole days, recording the 18900.00 standing value and the 120 guests standing on the booking.

The charge that answered it: 5670.00 raised 2026-09-10, three days after notice and inside the five-day posting window, and exactly the 30 percent ninety-to-thirty band on 18900.00 for notice 33 days out, which falls inside the 45-day free window but beyond thirty days.
The deposit held against that booking set against its charge: 5670.00 applied 2026-09-10 to the bill reference the charge carries, the notice having fallen inside the 45-day refundable window.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the single client organisation profile the call is about from the company name the caller gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Without the profile reference nothing else on the account can be retrieved, and the caller states no internal reference.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record a passing in-session identity check against the profile using the two details the caller reads out.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing may be quoted back about the account and no money may be moved on it until this has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the private event and banquet services agreement: its package, its state, the venue it is written against and the money held.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The package fixes every printed figure the two calculations use, and the agreement state decides whether the booking may be cancelled and charged at all.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole event ledger on the agreement: the booking entry and its estimate, the confirmed guarantee, the deposits, the other confirmed events still to be served, and the two cancellations already charged this year.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It supplies the estimated value and working count the contracted value falls back on, the guarantee entry that carries the guaranteed count, the event day and the room set-up, the count of confirmed events still standing in the diary, and the count of cancellation charges in the last twelve months.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the event request log on the agreement: which date and venue changes were asked for and which of them the desk approved.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The diary work charge rests on whether an approved venue change or an approved date change stands on the agreement, and two of the three requests on file were declined.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the corporate catering agreement the client also holds and its state.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The food value the contracted value is built on reads that account's orders, so the agreement it sits under has to be located first.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the catering orders on that account with their service days and values.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the order standing for the event's own day is added to the food value; the order for the day before and the one earlier in the month are not.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the client's own cancellation action so it can be handed to the caller.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The client calls the booking off herself, putting a cancellation entry on the event ledger with today as the day written notice was given and the contracted event value standing at that day.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the client may end her own confirmed event, and the contracted value the entry records is what the cancellation policy's calculation uniquely produces.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.banquet_agreement_id: The agreement row returned by the agreement lookup for this client: the only private event and banquet services agreement on the profile, written against venue VN-312 and standing active. Basis: the agreement lookup returns exactly this reference for the profile; uniqueness: no other banquet agreement exists on the account, so no other reference can be passed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The client organisation profile reference returned by the profile lookup for 'Northvale Life Sciences'. Basis: the profile lookup returns one matching profile and its reference; uniqueness: the caller identifies one company and one profile matches it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_reference: BQ-418206. Basis: the caller says 'the booking reference on her paperwork is BQ-418206', and the ledger carries a booking entry under exactly that reference for the seated dinner on 2026-09-27. Uniqueness: of the five bookings on the agreement only this one is the dinner on 27 September the caller is calling off; the other four stand on 2026-12-04, 2027-02-19, 2026-09-20 and 2026-10-10, and two of those are already cancelled.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.event_date: 2026-09-27, the day the event was to have been held. Basis: the booking entry for BQ-418206 in the event ledger carries event_date 2026-09-27, and the caller names 'the seated dinner on 27 September'. Uniqueness: the booking carries one event day, and the approved date change on file moved it to that day.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.contracted_value_usd: 69802.20 — the contracted event value standing at the day notice is given. A confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking and a catering order stands for the event's own day, so the food and beverage value is the guarantee's 45560.00 plus the 3250.00 breakfast served on 2026-09-27, that is 48810.00; the 1180.00 order for 2026-09-26 and the 2240.00 order for 2026-09-03 are not on the event day and do not count. The guarantee entry names a seated rounds set-up, so the audio-visual package 850.00 and the dance floor 650.00 stand in the value, 1500.00 together. The value the booking entry records, 40800.00, is above the package's room rental waiver spend of 12000.00, so no room rental stands. The guaranteed count 268 exceeds the working count 240 the booking was taken at, so the hours counted are 5.0 included plus 4.0 set-up lead plus 2.0 tear-down, that is 11.0; a guarantee stands and 268 reaches the smallest guest count 60, so staff are counted on 268 at one per 16 guests, 17 members at 42.00 an hour for 11.0 hours, that is 7854.00. The set-up is seated rounds and 268 reaches the smallest guest count, so half of the 1800.00 bar minimum stands, 900.00. The service charge is 22 percent of 48810.00, that is 10738.20. 48810.00 + 1500.00 + 0.00 + 7854.00 + 900.00 + 10738.20 = 69802.20.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.guaranteed_headcount: 268, the guest count standing on the booking at the day notice is given. Basis: the guarantee entry confirmed on 2026-09-19 carries guaranteed_headcount 268, and the guarantee replaces the working count of 240 the booking was taken at. Uniqueness: one guarantee entry stands on this booking, and a guarantee may never be lowered once given, so 268 is the only count standing.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's own action for raising the charge that falls due on the cancelled booking.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Raise the cancellation charge the policy yields against the agreement, carried on its own bill reference so the client can settle it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The charge is what the client rang about, and its amount is uniquely produced by the cancellation charge policy read on the ledger as it now stands.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.banquet_agreement_id: The same agreement reference the agreement lookup returned: the only banquet agreement on the profile. Basis: the agreement lookup returns exactly this reference; uniqueness: the cancelled booking sits under it and no other agreement exists on the account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The client organisation profile reference returned by the profile lookup. Basis: one profile matches 'Northvale Life Sciences'; uniqueness: the charge falls on the client whose agreement carries the booking.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.booking_reference: BQ-418206. Basis: the cancellation entry just registered carries booking_reference BQ-418206, and the tool return names it; uniqueness: the charge answers the booking that was cancelled, and only that booking carries a cancellation entry registered today.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.event_date: 2026-09-27, the day the cancelled event was to have been held. Basis: the cancellation entry carries event_date 2026-09-27; uniqueness: the entry records one event day.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.notice_given_date: 2026-09-22, the day written notice was given. Basis: the cancellation entry registered in the preceding action carries notice_given_date 2026-09-22 and its confirmation line states written notice was taken as given on 2026-09-22; uniqueness: the entry records one notice day, and it is the day of this call.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cancellation_charge_usd: 53211.65 — the charge the cancelled booking carries. Notice was given on 2026-09-22 for an event on 2026-09-27, five whole calendar days, which is inside seven days, so the notice percentage is the within-seven-days percentage, 90. The agreement has carried two cancellation charges in the twelve months ending today, on 2026-08-28 and on 2026-09-10, so the repeat percentage is the higher uplift, 10. 90 plus 10 is 100, held to 100, worked on the 69802.20 the cancellation entry records: 69802.20. Two confirmed events that have neither been delivered nor cancelled still stand on the agreement, the reception on 2026-12-04 and the dinner on 2027-02-19, so the charge is reduced by a quarter: 52351.65. The count standing in the cancellation entry, 268, passes the package's security threshold of 250 and notice was inside seven days, so licensed security stands at 52.00 an hour for the 5.0 service hours included, 260.00. The event request log carries an approved date change on the agreement and no approved venue change, so the date change charge of 600.00 is added. 52351.65 + 260.00 + 600.00 = 53211.65.

factor_trace: committed_food_value (method): the guarantee entry posted 2026-09-19 prices to 45560.00 and one catering order, 3250.00 served on 2026-09-27, stands for the event's own day, so both tier conditions hold and the food value is 48810.00; the baseline reads the booking entry's own estimate, 40800.00, and would give 60030.00.

contracted_room_extras (parameter): the guarantee entry is built to a seated_rounds set-up, so the tier selects the audio-visual package 850.00 with the dance floor 650.00, 1500.00; the baseline carries no extras at all and would give 68302.20.

room_rental_standing (parameter): the booking entry records 40800.00, above the 12000.00 waiver spend, so the tier selects no room rental; the baseline charges the printed 950.00 rental and would give 70752.20.

contracted_hours_counted (method): a guarantee entry stands and its 268 exceeds the 240 the booking was taken at, so the hours counted are 5.0 + 4.0 + 2.0 = 11.0; the baseline counts the 5.0 included hours alone and would give 65518.20.

contracted_staffing (parameter): a guarantee stands and 268 reaches the smallest guest count 60, so staff are counted on 268 at one per 16 up to the next whole member, 17 at 42.00 for 11.0 hours = 7854.00; the baseline carries no contracted staffing and would give 61948.20.

bar_element_standing (parameter): the set-up is seated_rounds and the count standing, 268, reaches the smallest guest count, so the seated share of the 1800.00 bar minimum stands, 900.00; the baseline carries no bar element and would give 68902.20.

unowned bindings: booked_value 40800.00 and booked_count 240 are plain reads of the booking entry; service_charge_usd is 22 percent of the food value, 10738.20; result adds the six parts and rounds once at the end.

the room stands set for seated rounds or for a reception
the food and beverage value standing on the booking entry reaches the room rental waiver spend printed against the package
a confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking and the count it guarantees exceeds the working count the booking was taken at
a confirmed guarantee entry stands on the booking and the count it guarantees reaches the smallest guest count printed against the package
the room stands set for seated rounds and the count standing on the booking reaches the smallest guest count printed against the package

factor_trace: notice_percentage (parameter): the cancellation entry registered at this call carries notice_given_date 2026-09-22 against an event day of 2026-09-27, five days, so the within-seven-days percentage 90 applies; the baseline reads the thirty-to-seven percentage 60 and would give 37506.15.

repeat_cancellation_percentage (parameter): two cancellation charges stand on the agreement inside the twelve months ending today, posted 2026-08-28 and 2026-09-10, so the higher uplift of 10 applies; the baseline carries no repeat percentage and would give 47976.49.

remaining_diary_relief (method): five booking entries stand on the agreement, none delivered and three cancelled once this cancellation is registered, so two confirmed events remain and the charge is reduced by a quarter; the baseline leaves the banded charge as worked and would give 70662.20.

security_standdown (parameter): the cancellation entry carries 268 guests, above the 250 security threshold, and notice fell inside seven days, so 52.00 an hour stands for the 5.0 included service hours, 260.00; the baseline carries no security and would give 52951.65.

diary_work_charge (parameter): the event request log carries one approved date change on the agreement and no approved venue change, so the 600.00 date change charge is added; the two declined requests do not count, and the baseline adds nothing and would give 52611.65.

unowned bindings: contracted_value reads 69802.20 from the cancellation entry the preceding write put on the ledger; effective_pct is 90 + 10 held to 100; banded_charge_usd is 69802.20; result adds the reduced charge, the security and the diary work charge and rounds once.

the agreement has already carried two or more cancellation charges in the twelve months ending on the day the charge is raised
two or more confirmed events that have neither been delivered nor cancelled stand on the agreement
written notice was given inside seven days of the event and the count standing in the cancellation entry passes the security threshold printed against the package

edges.condition: A banquet_ledger row of event family banquet_booking_cancelled stands for the booking, carrying notice_given_date and the contracted amount_usd standing at that day.
edges.policy_source: The charge for a cancelled event is not fixed until the event ledger carries, for that booking, a cancellation entry recording the day written notice was given and the contracted event value standing at that day.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-09-22 10:20:00 EDT the event ledger carries no cancellation entry for booking BQ-418206 at all: the only rows under that reference are the booking entry, its two deposits and its confirmed guarantee. The two cancellation entries that do stand on the agreement belong to other bookings, so the value the charge is worked on reads 22400.00 from an unrelated booking and the notice span reads 2026-09-07 to 2026-10-10 instead of this booking's.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The client's own cancellation write puts a banquet_booking_cancelled row on the ledger for BQ-418206 with notice_given_date 2026-09-22, event_date 2026-09-27, amount_usd 69802.20 and 268 guests; contracted_value then reads 69802.20, notice_days reads 5 and cancelled_count reads 268.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has one edge and therefore one topological order: the client's cancellation write, then the charge. There are no parallel prerequisites to reorder. The order is not a convention: the charge policy's own rule says its result is not fixed until a cancellation entry with a notice day and a standing value is on the ledger, and the recomputation confirms the dependence - with the cancellation written first the charge is 53211.65, with it skipped the same formula yields 7320.00.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the client's cancellation write and replaying everything else leaves the charge policy reading the most recent cancellation entry on the agreement, the one for BQ-409883: contracted_value 22400.00 (the largest standing cancelled value), notice span 2026-09-07 to 2026-10-10 giving 33 days and a 30 percent band, and cancelled_count 140, which does not pass the security threshold. cancellation_charge_usd moves from 53211.65 to 7320.00.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never names the cancellation entry, the notice day, the need for the client to end the booking herself, or any step before the charge. What the caller raises is the money question - what Northvale will be charged for pulling out this late and having it on the books today - plus the plain fact that the dinner is not going ahead. The only sentence touching the client's own act is a passive reaction that fires after the agent has already explained it: 'When the agent explains that calling the booking off is something Northvale has to do itself and offers to put it in front of her, she takes it without fuss'. She never asks whether something has to be sorted first, never mentions written notice, and if the agent posts nothing she does not prompt.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_cancellation_charge_5262dfa3 in task_tools.py reads nothing before it writes: its body computes a row id from its arguments, mints a bill reference and calls ctx.create on banquet_ledger. It never looks for a cancellation entry, never validates that one exists, raises no error and returns the same confirmation line whether or not the prerequisite is resolved. Called on the opening world it writes a charge happily - it would simply be the wrong amount, which is exactly where the consequence shows up: in the terminal hash.
